title: IA HF2635: A bill for an act relating to health carriers standards of conduct; utilization review organizations, artificial intelligence, audits, and prior authorizations; certificate of need processes; and including applicability provisions. (Formerly HF 2438.) Effective date: 07/01/2026.

obligations: A utilization review organization that conducts an audit shall notify the health care provider of the initiation of the audit no later than fifteen calendar days after selecting the claim for audit (Sec. 3, 514F.8C(2)(a)).
A utilization review organization shall complete an audit and issue a determination no later than forty five calendar days after receiving all requested documentation (Sec. 3, 514F.8C(2)(b)).
A utilization review organization shall consider an appeal and issue a final determination no later than thirty calendar days after receiving notice of the appeal (Sec. 3, 514F.8C(2)(d)).

A health care provider shall submit all requests for prior authorization to a health carrier electronically using a standards based application programming interface or another compliant electronic submission supported by the health carrier (Sec. 5, 514F.8(6A)(a)).

A utilization review organization shall not deny or downgrade a prior authorization request unless the decision is made by a qualified reviewer or clinical peer and the organization provides a written statement, written appeals explanation, and written attestation (Sec. 6, 514F.8A(2)).

At the request of the requesting health care provider, a utilization review organization that denies a request shall conduct a consultation within seven business days with a qualified reviewer or clinical peer (Sec. 6, 514F.8A(3)).

An appeal of a denial or downgrade shall be conducted by a qualified reviewer or clinical peer who was not involved in the initial determination, and the reviewer shall consider known clinical aspects, medical records, and relevant medical literature (Sec. 6, 514F.8A(4)).

A health care provider submitting a prior authorization request to a managed care organization shall submit the request electronically using a standards based application programming interface or another compliant electronic submission (Sec. 10, 249A.6(1)).

A new institutional health service or changed institutional health service shall not be offered or developed without prior application to the department and receipt of a certificate of need (Sec. 15, 135.62(1)(a)).

An applicant for a certificate of need shall submit an application on forms furnished or prescribed by the department, containing required information, and accompanied by the required fee (Sec. 15, 135.62(1)(b), (c)).
The department shall examine a certificate of need application for form and completeness within fifteen business days and accept or reject it (Sec. 20, 135.65(1)(a)).
Upon acceptance of an application, the department shall notify all affected persons in writing through electronic means that formal review has been initiated (Sec. 20, 135.65(2)).
The department may waive the letter of intent procedures and conduct a summary review for projects meeting specified criteria (Sec. 23, 135.66(1)).
Upon expiration of a certificate of need, any affected person may submit relevant information to the department, and the department may call a public hearing (Sec. 24, 135.70(2)).

The department shall adopt rules including criteria for determining when it is not feasible to complete formal review within the time limit, and any deferral shall not exceed thirty calendar days unless both applicant and department agree (Sec. 25, 135.71(4)).
prohibitions: A utilization review organization shall not use an artificial intelligence based algorithm or system as the sole basis for a decision to deny, delay, or downgrade a prior authorization request for a health care service based on medical necessity (Sec. 2, 514F.8(2A)).

A health carrier shall not impose any financial penalty, reimbursement reduction, administrative fee, or terminate a provider's participation based on the provider's referral to or affiliation with an out of network health care provider (Sec. 4, 514F.8D(2)).
A health carrier shall not interfere with or participate in a health care provider's decisions regarding staffing and referrals, except as otherwise provided by law (Sec. 4, 514F.8D(3)).
A health carrier shall not offer, attempt to enforce, or enforce an agreement with a health care provider without providing an opportunity for negotiation (Sec. 4, 514F.8D(4)).
A utilization review organization shall not deny or downgrade a request for prior authorization unless all requirements of section 514F.8A are met (Sec. 6, 514F.8A(2)).

A health carrier shall not require prior authorization for, or impose additional utilization review requirements on, a covered person for a cancer related screening recommended per NCCN guidelines category 2A or lower, or for diagnosis and treatment of an emergency medical condition during inpatient care if life threatening (Sec. 7, 514F.8B(2)).

The department or a managed care organization shall not require prior authorization for, or impose additional utilization review requirements on, a medical assistance recipient for the same cancer related screenings and emergency medical conditions (Sec. 9, 249A.5(2)).

The department or a managed care organization shall not require prior authorization for, or impose additional utilization review requirements on, an eligible child under the Hawki program for the same cancer related screenings and emergency medical conditions (Sec. 11, 514I.13(2)).

What it does

This Iowa law regulates health carriers and utilization review organizations in prior authorization, audits, artificial intelligence use, and provider standards of conduct. It prohibits using artificial intelligence as the sole basis to deny, delay, or downgrade medical necessity prior authorizations, sets audit and peer review timelines, and exempts certain cancer screenings and emergency conditions from prior authorization. It also updates certificate of need thresholds and exemptions and provides enforcement through the insurance commissioner.

Who it applies to

  • Health carriers
  • Utilization review organizations
  • Health care providers
  • Managed care organizations contracting with the Iowa department of health and human services
  • The Iowa department of health and human services
  • Institutional health facilities and other entities subject to certificate of need
  • Health maintenance organizations
  • Third party payment providers offering specified health coverage in Iowa

Effective date

07/01/2026

Key definitions

  • Downgrade: a decision by a utilization review organization to change an expedited or urgent request for prior authorization to a standard determination, or otherwise modify a health care service that is the subject of a request for prior authorization to a lower level health care service (Sec. 1, 514F.8(1)(0b)).
  • Audit: a review, investigation, or request for additional documentation by a utilization review organization before or after issuing payment on a claim to a health care provider (Sec. 3, 514F.8C(1)(a)).
  • Clinical peer: a health care professional who practices in the same or similar specialty as the requesting provider, has experience managing the specific medical condition or administering the health care service, and is employed by or contracted with the utilization review organization or health carrier (Sec. 6, 514F.8A(1)(a)).
  • Qualified reviewer: a physician who practices in the same or a similar specialty as the requesting provider, has training and expertise to treat the specific medical condition including sufficient knowledge to determine medical necessity or clinical appropriateness, and is employed by or contracted with the utilization review organization (Sec. 6, 514F.8A(1)(j)).
  • Prior authorization for medical assistance: any process used by the department or a managed care organization to determine if, before a health care service is furnished to a recipient, the service is covered or medically necessary (Sec. 9, 249A.5(1)(c)).
  • Emergency medical condition: same as defined in 42 C.F.R. section 438.114 (Sec. 7, 514F.8B(1)(b); Sec. 9, 249A.5(1)(a); Sec. 11, 514I.13(1)(a)).
  • Institutional health facility: any of the following without regard to public or private ownership, for profit status, or sponsorship by a health maintenance organization: a hospital as defined in section 135B.1, a health care facility as defined in section 135C.1, an organized outpatient health facility as defined in section 135.61, an ambulatory surgical center as defined in section 135.61, or a community mental health center as defined in section 225A.1 (Sec. 27, 135P.1(3A)).
  • New institutional health service or changed institutional health service: includes construction, development, or establishment of a new institutional health facility above specified dollar thresholds, relocation of an institutional health facility, capital expenditures, leases, or donations above specified thresholds, permanent bed capacity changes, new health services above five hundred thousand dollars, deletion or relocation of health services, acquisition of equipment above one million five hundred thousand dollars resulting in new services above thresholds, mobile health services above four million five hundred thousand dollars, and specified services including cardiac catheterization, open heart surgical, organ transplantation, and radiation therapy (Sec. 14, 135.61(16)).

Obligations

  • A utilization review organization that conducts an audit shall notify the health care provider of the initiation of the audit no later than fifteen calendar days after selecting the claim for audit (Sec. 3, 514F.8C(2)(a)).
  • A utilization review organization shall complete an audit and issue a determination no later than forty five calendar days after receiving all requested documentation (Sec. 3, 514F.8C(2)(b)).
  • A utilization review organization shall consider an appeal and issue a final determination no later than thirty calendar days after receiving notice of the appeal (Sec. 3, 514F.8C(2)(d)).
  • A health care provider shall submit all requests for prior authorization to a health carrier electronically using a standards based application programming interface or another compliant electronic submission supported by the health carrier (Sec. 5, 514F.8(6A)(a)).
  • A utilization review organization shall not deny or downgrade a prior authorization request unless the decision is made by a qualified reviewer or clinical peer and the organization provides a written statement, written appeals explanation, and written attestation (Sec. 6, 514F.8A(2)).
  • At the request of the requesting health care provider, a utilization review organization that denies a request shall conduct a consultation within seven business days with a qualified reviewer or clinical peer (Sec. 6, 514F.8A(3)).
  • An appeal of a denial or downgrade shall be conducted by a qualified reviewer or clinical peer who was not involved in the initial determination, and the reviewer shall consider known clinical aspects, medical records, and relevant medical literature (Sec. 6, 514F.8A(4)).
  • A health care provider submitting a prior authorization request to a managed care organization shall submit the request electronically using a standards based application programming interface or another compliant electronic submission (Sec. 10, 249A.6(1)).
  • A new institutional health service or changed institutional health service shall not be offered or developed without prior application to the department and receipt of a certificate of need (Sec. 15, 135.62(1)(a)).
  • An applicant for a certificate of need shall submit an application on forms furnished or prescribed by the department, containing required information, and accompanied by the required fee (Sec. 15, 135.62(1)(b), (c)).
  • The department shall examine a certificate of need application for form and completeness within fifteen business days and accept or reject it (Sec. 20, 135.65(1)(a)).
  • Upon acceptance of an application, the department shall notify all affected persons in writing through electronic means that formal review has been initiated (Sec. 20, 135.65(2)).
  • The department may waive the letter of intent procedures and conduct a summary review for projects meeting specified criteria (Sec. 23, 135.66(1)).
  • Upon expiration of a certificate of need, any affected person may submit relevant information to the department, and the department may call a public hearing (Sec. 24, 135.70(2)).
  • The department shall adopt rules including criteria for determining when it is not feasible to complete formal review within the time limit, and any deferral shall not exceed thirty calendar days unless both applicant and department agree (Sec. 25, 135.71(4)).

Prohibitions

  • A utilization review organization shall not use an artificial intelligence based algorithm or system as the sole basis for a decision to deny, delay, or downgrade a prior authorization request for a health care service based on medical necessity (Sec. 2, 514F.8(2A)).
  • A health carrier shall not impose any financial penalty, reimbursement reduction, administrative fee, or terminate a provider's participation based on the provider's referral to or affiliation with an out of network health care provider (Sec. 4, 514F.8D(2)).
  • A health carrier shall not interfere with or participate in a health care provider's decisions regarding staffing and referrals, except as otherwise provided by law (Sec. 4, 514F.8D(3)).
  • A health carrier shall not offer, attempt to enforce, or enforce an agreement with a health care provider without providing an opportunity for negotiation (Sec. 4, 514F.8D(4)).
  • A utilization review organization shall not deny or downgrade a request for prior authorization unless all requirements of section 514F.8A are met (Sec. 6, 514F.8A(2)).
  • A health carrier shall not require prior authorization for, or impose additional utilization review requirements on, a covered person for a cancer related screening recommended per NCCN guidelines category 2A or lower, or for diagnosis and treatment of an emergency medical condition during inpatient care if life threatening (Sec. 7, 514F.8B(2)).
  • The department or a managed care organization shall not require prior authorization for, or impose additional utilization review requirements on, a medical assistance recipient for the same cancer related screenings and emergency medical conditions (Sec. 9, 249A.5(2)).
  • The department or a managed care organization shall not require prior authorization for, or impose additional utilization review requirements on, an eligible child under the Hawki program for the same cancer related screenings and emergency medical conditions (Sec. 11, 514I.13(2)).
  • A new institutional health service or changed institutional health service shall not be offered or developed without a certificate of need (Sec. 15, 135.62(1)(a)).

Penalties and enforcement

The commissioner of insurance enforces sections 514F.8, 514F.8A, 514F.8B, 514F.8C, and 514F.8D using remedies authorized by chapters 505 and 507B and procedures in sections 507B.6, 507B.7, and 507B.8. Upon a finding of a pattern or practice of noncompliance, the commissioner may suspend a utilization review organization's authority to conduct utilization review. If after a hearing the commissioner finds a utilization review organization violated the audit requirements, the claim shall be approved and promptly paid including interest at ten percent per annum. The statute does not state a private right of action. (Sec. 8, 514F.8E; Sec. 3, 514F.8C(2)(e))

How it affects AI deployment

  • An organization deploying artificial intelligence in utilization review may use it only for initial review of prior authorization requests, not as the sole basis to deny, delay, or downgrade a medical necessity based request (Sec. 2, 514F.8(2A)).
  • Any denial or downgrade decision must be made by a qualified reviewer or clinical peer, and the organization must provide a written statement signed by that reviewer, a written appeals explanation, and a written attestation of the reviewer's qualifications (Sec. 6, 514F.8A(2)).
  • Artificial intelligence systems used in prior authorization workflows must support electronic submission through a standards based application programming interface or other compliant electronic method (Sec. 5, 514F.8(6A); Sec. 10, 249A.6).
  • Organizations using artificial intelligence remain subject to audit timelines, appeal rights, and enforcement, including suspension of utilization review authority for a pattern or practice of noncompliance (Sec. 3, 514F.8C; Sec. 8, 514F.8E).

Notable exemptions

  • The audit requirements do not apply to accident only, specified disease, short term hospital or medical, hospital confinement indemnity, credit, dental, vision, Medicare supplement, long term care, basic hospital and medical surgical expense coverage, disability income, liability supplement, workers compensation or similar insurance, or automobile medical payment insurance (Sec. 3, 514F.8C(4)(b)).
  • The audit requirements do not apply to a claim under active fraud investigation by a state or federal authority (Sec. 3, 514F.8C(6)(b)).
  • The prior authorization peer review requirements do not apply to the same list of excepted coverages (Sec. 6, 514F.8A(6)(b)).
  • The prior authorization exemptions do not apply to the same list of excepted coverages (Sec. 7, 514F.8B(4)(b)).
  • Certificate of need review does not apply to private offices and private clinics of individual physicians, dentists, or other practitioners or groups of health care providers, except as provided by section 135.61(16)(e) and section 135.61(2) and (18) (Sec. 16, 135.62(2)(a)).
  • A health maintenance organization is exempt from certificate of need except when it constructs, develops, renovates, relocates, or otherwise establishes an institutional health facility or acquires major medical equipment as provided by section 135.61(16)(f) (Sec. 16, 135.62(2)(e)).
  • New certificate of need exemptions include organized outpatient health facilities providing behavioral health services including substitution based treatment centers for opiate addiction, open heart surgical services, organ transplantation services, radiation therapy services, and cardiac catheterization services (Sec. 18, 135.62(2)(r) through (v)).
  • Summary review is available for projects limited to disaster repair or replacement, compliance with licensing or safety requirements, bed capacity changes of ten percent or ten beds or less over two years, total cost not exceeding one hundred fifty thousand dollars, or other projects agreed to by the department (Sec. 23, 135.66(1)(a) through (e)).
  • Intermediate care facilities for persons with an intellectual disability or mental illness are exempt from the certificate of need application fee (Sec. 15, 135.62(1)(c)(1)).

Compliance steps

  • Determine whether the organization is a health carrier, utilization review organization, managed care organization, or institutional health facility subject to the act (Sec. 3, 514F.8C(4); Sec. 4, 514F.8D; Sec. 6, 514F.8A(6); Sec. 7, 514F.8B(4); Sec. 9, 249A.5(3); Sec. 11, 514I.13(3); Sec. 15, 135.62(1)).
  • If using artificial intelligence in prior authorization, configure the system to perform only initial review and ensure a qualified reviewer or clinical peer makes any denial or downgrade decision (Sec. 2, 514F.8(2A); Sec. 6, 514F.8A(2)).
  • Implement written denial and downgrade procedures that include a signed statement, appeals explanation, and attestation from the qualified reviewer or clinical peer (Sec. 6, 514F.8A(2)(b)).
  • Establish audit workflows with fifteen day initiation notice, forty five day completion, thirty day appeal consideration, and electronic delivery opt in (Sec. 3, 514F.8C(2), (3)).
  • Enable electronic prior authorization submission through a standards based application programming interface or compliant method by July 1, 2027 (Sec. 5, 514F.8(6A); Sec. 10, 249A.6).
  • Remove prior authorization requirements for cancer related screenings recommended per NCCN category 2A or lower and for emergency medical conditions during inpatient care (Sec. 7, 514F.8B(2); Sec. 9, 249A.5(2); Sec. 11, 514I.13(2)).
  • Review provider contracts to eliminate financial penalties, reimbursement reductions, administrative fees, termination based on out of network referrals, interference with staffing and referrals, and non negotiable agreements (Sec. 4, 514F.8D(2) through (4)).
  • For certificate of need, evaluate whether a project exceeds the new dollar thresholds or falls under a new exemption, and if required, submit an application with the fee and obtain a certificate before offering or developing the service (Sec. 14, 135.61(16); Sec. 15, 135.62(1); Sec. 18, 135.62(2)(r) through (v)).
  • Prepare for commissioner enforcement by maintaining records of compliance and responding to proceedings under chapters 505 and 507B, and avoid a pattern or practice of noncompliance to prevent suspension of utilization review authority (Sec. 8, 514F.8E).
